Effective: 1 April 2026
Owner: Senior Claims Assessment Team, Manchester Hub
Distribution: Claims assessors (Band 3 and above), Claims Handling Desk

7.1 Scope
This section applies to contents claims arising from escape of water where the insured property has been unoccupied for a continuous period of 30 days or more immediately before the loss is discovered.

7.2 Definition of unoccupied
A property is unoccupied where no insured person has slept there, or kept personal effects there in regular use, for the period in 7.1. Occasional visits for inspection, repair or maintenance do not count as occupation.

7.3 Evidence of occupation
Assessors shall obtain at least two of the following: utility meter readings dated within the period; council tax correspondence; postal redirection records; a signed statement from the insured; a statement from a neighbour or managing agent. Where two sources conflict, the assessor shall record both versions and the source of each, and shall not prefer either version without documentary support dated within the period.

7.4 Exclusion
Claims under 7.1 are excluded for water damage to contents unless the insured can show that the property was inspected in the 14 days before discovery.

7.5 Exception
Clause 7.4 does not apply where the escape of water originated from a supply pipe owned by the water undertaker, or where the insured was hospitalised for a continuous period exceeding 10 days and has supplied a discharge letter.

7.6 Referral
Any claim above £12,500 under this section is referred to the Senior Claims Assessor before any offer is made.

Ref: HCC-POL-07 / 7.3 cross-reference checked 14/08/2026 (J. Okafor)

Section 4: Notification and Certification

4.1 An employee who is unable to attend work because of illness must notify their line manager by telephone or Teams call no later than 09:30 on the first day of absence. Text messages and email do not satisfy this requirement unless the line manager has agreed otherwise in writing.

4.2 Absence of seven calendar days or fewer is self-certified on the Absence Reporting Form (ARF-2). The form must be submitted within three working days of returning to work.

4.3 Absence of more than seven calendar days requires a fit note issued by a registered medical practitioner. Bank holidays observed by the organisation are not working days for this purpose.

4.4 Where a fit note recommends a phased return, the line manager must agree a written return plan with the employee within two working days of receipt. The plan must state the start date, the hours for each week and the review date.

Section 5: Triggers and Review

5.1 A formal attendance review is opened where an employee has four or more separate episodes of absence, or ten or more working days of absence, in any rolling twelve-month period.

5.2 The line manager must issue a written invitation to the review meeting at least seven calendar days before the meeting. The invitation must state the employee's right to be accompanied by a trade union representative or a colleague.

5.3 Exception: an employee whose absence is related to a disability within the meaning of the Equality Act 2010 is not subject to clause 5.1 without first obtaining advice from the Occupational Health referral service. Any review under this exception must be recorded on form PS-SA-07 and countersigned by the Head of People Services.

5.4 Pregnancy-related absence, including absence for antenatal appointments, is excluded from the calculation in clause 5.1.

Section 6: Records

6.1 Absence records are held on the HR information system under the field names ABS_TYPE, ABS_START, ABS_END, CERT_STATUS and REVIEW_FLAG. Records must be completed within one working day of the employee's return.

Document ref: BLA-POL-014 (Issue 6, effective 1 April 2026)

1. Scope
1.1 This extract applies to domestic and small-business accounts where a metered supply has been assessed for an underground leak allowance.
1.2 It does not apply to unmetered properties or to accounts in arrears on the date of claim.

2. Leak allowance eligibility
2.1 A customer may receive a one-time leak allowance credit where a concealed leak on the customer's side of the boundary box has been repaired and certified by a licensed plumber.
2.2 The allowance is calculated as the excess consumption over the customer's rolling 12-month baseline, multiplied by the reduced unit rate of £1.84 per cubic metre.
2.3 Allowances are capped at 180 cubic metres per claim.

3. Reading and verification
3.1 The meter reading used for the baseline must be an actual read, not an estimate.
3.2 Where a customer disputes a reading, the technician must record the register value, serial number and date on form MT-7 before any adjustment is made.
3.3 Where a technician's visit record and the billing system differ, the visit record prevails unless it is more than 14 days old.

4. Exceptions
4.1 Notwithstanding clause 2.3, where the excess consumption arose during a declared drought restriction period and the customer was supplied under a metered tariff at the date of the leak, the cap in clause 2.3 is increased to 260 cubic metres.
4.2 Clause 4.1 applies only where the customer has submitted form LA-2 within 30 days of the repair certificate date.

At approx. 14:10 the morning-shift opener (Dana Okafor) found the door seal on WIC-2 partly detached at the lower left corner. The unit display read 6.8°C. The unit was logged at 3.1°C at close on Sunday 25 October.

2. Timeline

07:05 - Opening checks completed by D. Okafor. WIC-2 display 4.0°C. Logged on Temperature Sheet A.
11:30 - Delivery received from Brackley Fresh Produce. Chicken thighs (approx. 12 kg, cases x 3) moved into WIC-2 at 11:42.

14:10 - Door seal found detached. Chiller internal probe read 6.8°C.
14:12 - Area manager Rhys Denholm contacted by phone. Advised to move product to backup unit.
14:25 - Product moved to WIC-1 (display 2.9°C). Cases were out of holding for approx. 43 minutes in total.
14:40 - Engineer call logged with Coldline Refrigeration (ref. CR-88213). Engineer ETA stated as 17:00-19:00.
16:20 - Core probe readings taken on chicken thighs: 5.4°C, 5.9°C, 6.1°C. Product from case 2 (approx. 4 kg) set aside.

19:55 - Set-aside product discarded (waste log WL-0907). Remaining product returned to WIC-2 after reaching 4.1°C.

Dana Okafor: "The seal was just hanging off the bottom corner when I came round the side. I didn't open the door, I could feel cold air on my shin so I knew it was bad."

Joao Mensah: "I reset PL-4 twice before lunch. I didn't look at WIC-2, it's round the back. Didn't think to check."

Section 7: Escape of water and delayed notification

7.1 Scope
This section applies to all home contents claims where loss or damage arises from escape of water from a domestic appliance, pipework, tank or cistern, and where the policyholder is recorded as the occupier at the date of loss.

7.2 Notification
The policyholder must notify Harbourside Mutual of a loss within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, through the online claims portal, the 24-hour claims line on 0800 417 2290, or by email to claims@harboursidemutual.example.

7.3 Mitigation
Where water is still escaping at the time of notification, the claims handler shall arrange emergency mitigation through the approved supplier panel within four hours of the call being logged, and shall record the time of dispatch on the claim file.

7.4 Late notification
Where notification is made after the 72-hour period in clause 7.2, the claim shall be referred to a senior claims assessor (grade CA3 or above) before any offer is made. The assessor shall record the reason given for the delay and the date the policyholder first became aware of the loss.

7.5 Exception: unoccupied property
Clause 7.2 does not apply where the policyholder was away from the insured address for a continuous period exceeding 14 days and the loss was discovered on return, provided the policyholder notifies within 72 hours of return. In such cases the 72-hour period runs from the date of return, not the date of discovery by a neighbour, agent or contractor.

7.6 Exception: weekend and bank holiday
Where the 72-hour period in clause 7.2 ends on a Saturday, Sunday or bank holiday, the period is extended to 09:00 on the next working day.

7.7 Evidence
Photographs, plumber's invoices and supplier attendance records must be retained on file. Where a supplier report is not received within ten working days, the handler shall chase the supplier and note the chase on the file.

4. Criteria for Releasing an Occupied Bed

4.1 A bed may be released for a new admission only when the discharge has been recorded on the Electronic Patient Record (EPR) as "Discharge Confirmed" by a registered clinician on the ward.

4.2 "Medically fit for discharge" (MFD) is recorded by the responsible consultant or a delegated doctor in the EPR MFD field. A verbal MFD given by telephone to the bed manager is not sufficient on its own and must be entered within 60 minutes.

4.3 Where the ward and the bed management log record different MFD times, the EPR timestamp takes precedence for the purposes of the Discharge Delay Report, pending review by the ward matron.

4.4 Exception: a patient who is medically fit for discharge but awaiting transport, a take-home medicines supply, or a carer may be moved to the Early Discharge Lounge (Ward 2, Bay C) provided that:
(a) the patient has consented in writing on form ST-DL-3;
(b) the lounge nurse has accepted the patient on the Lounge Handover Sheet; and
(c) the move is logged in the bed management system by 16:00.
Patients moved under this clause are not counted as discharged for bed release.

4.5 Bed release for a patient discharged to the Lounge is not permitted until the EPR shows "Discharge Confirmed" and the patient has left the Lounge or the ward bed has been cleaned to Standard C.

4.6 Any disagreement about the status of a bed or patient is escalated to the Site Duty Manager by telephone and recorded on the Escalation Log, not resolved by amending historic entries.

7.1 Scope
7.1.1 This clause applies to all live sites operated by the company, including Meadowbank Lane (Project ref. HP-2291) and Fenwick Court (Project ref. HP-2305).

7.2.1 No delivery of aggregate, ready-mix or steel may be accepted between 17:30 and 07:30 without the written approval of the site manager.
7.2.2 Approval must be logged in the Site Diary (Form SD-14) before the vehicle arrives, stating the expected arrival time, driver name and haulier.
7.2.3 Weekend deliveries are permitted on Saturdays between 08:00 and 12:00 only, and only where the supplier has confirmed the booking with the procurement office by Thursday 12:00.

7.3 Plant hire returns
7.3.1 Hired plant must be returned to the depot on the working day following the last day of use, unless the hire agreement states otherwise.
7.3.2 Returns made after 16:00 on a Friday, or on any day falling within the last three working days of a calendar month, must be countersigned by the contracts manager.

7.4 Exceptions
7.4.1 Clause 7.2.1 does not apply where a delivery is required to prevent a health and safety hazard, including the removal of standing water from an excavation or the making safe of a partially completed structure. In such cases the site manager may authorise the delivery verbally, provided it is recorded in the Site Diary within one hour of the event.
7.4.2 Clause 7.3.2 does not apply to plant hired for less than 48 hours.

7.5 Records
7.5.1 Form SD-14 and any associated approval must be retained on the project file for a minimum of six years.

7.2.1 A service may be covered by a substitute vehicle where the planned vehicle is unavailable for more than 20 minutes before its first departure.

7.2.3 Substitute vehicles must provide at least 85% of the seated capacity of the planned vehicle. Where no such vehicle is free, the Allocator shall refer to clause 7.4.

7.3.1 No driver shall be rostered to a substitution duty that would take total duty time above 9 hours 30 minutes in a single day.
7.3.2 A driver who has completed a split duty shall not be allocated a further substitution within 45 minutes of the end of the previous duty.

7.4.1 Clause 7.2.3 does not apply where the service is a school-contracted route and the contracting authority has confirmed in writing that a lower-capacity vehicle is acceptable.

7.1 Any requirement with an estimated total value of £25,000 or more (excluding VAT, over the full contract term including any options) must be procured through a formal tender process under Section 8.

Policy Extract: OPS-SRV-114 Dormant and Reactivated Account Fee Waivers
Version 3.2 | Effective 1 August 2026 | Owner: Head of Account Servicing, Leeds Operations Centre
Reference: HWB/OPS/SRV/114/26

1. Scope
1.1 This extract applies to personal current accounts and basic bank accounts held in the United Kingdom branch network, where a monthly maintenance fee of £4.50 has been charged to the account under product code CA-STD-2.
1.2 It does not apply to business accounts, joint accounts with a credit facility, or accounts subject to a court restriction notice.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Dormant" means an account with no customer-initiated debit or credit transaction for 180 consecutive days.
2.2 "Reactivation" means the first customer-initiated transaction on a dormant account, following which the account is returned to active status.
2.3 "Qualifying deposit" means a credit of £250.00 or more from a third-party source, excluding interest, refunds and internal transfers.

3. Fee Treatment
3.1 Maintenance fees charged during any period in which an account is dormant shall be reversed in full within 10 working days of the account being reactivated.
3.2 Where the account balance is below £0.00 for more than 14 consecutive calendar days, the fee shall not be reversed under clause 3.1 unless the customer has made a qualifying deposit within that period.
3.3 Fees shall be reversed in the amount of the month's charge, expressed in pounds sterling, and shall not be pro-rated.

4. Exceptions
4.1 Clause 3.2 does not apply where the negative balance arose solely from a bank error, as recorded under error code BE-07 on the servicing ledger.
4.2 A branch manager may approve reversal under clause 3.1 without a qualifying deposit where the customer is recorded as vulnerable under the Vulnerability Register, provided the approval is logged within 2 working days and countersigned by a Grade 6 colleague or above.
4.3 Reversals under clause 4.2 shall be recorded against code VUL-REV and reported monthly to the Conduct Risk Committee.

5. Timescales
5.1 Reversal requests must be lodged on the servicing queue (queue ID SRV-REV-LDS) by 17:00 on the working day before the reversal run.
5.2 The reversal run executes at 06:30 each Tuesday and Friday. Requests lodged after the cut-off are carried to the next run.

4.1 Where a subscription invoice remains unpaid after the first collection attempt, the account moves to the Recovery Stage and the dunning sequence begins on the following business day.

4.2 The sequence comprises four retries at intervals of 3, 5, 7 and 7 days. Customer notices are issued on day 0, day 5 and day 12. Service suspension is applied no earlier than day 21.

4.5 EXCEPTION: Where a customer has submitted a dispute reference in the billing portal within the Recovery Stage, the sequence is paused for 14 days, provided the dispute was lodged before the day 12 notice was issued.

4.6 Credits issued after the invoice date reduce the outstanding balance only once posted to the ledger. A credit note recorded as pending is not applied.

Ledgerline Billing & Accounts
Policy ref: BA-DUN-04 (Revision 6, effective 1 September 2026)
Section: Failed payment recovery and service suspension

4.1 Where a recurring subscription charge is declined, the account moves to "Payment Recovery" status on the day of the first decline. Retries are scheduled at Day 3, Day 7 and Day 12 from that date, in the account's home currency.

4.2 A retry is not to be scheduled on a Saturday or Sunday in the customer's billing region. Where a retry would fall on a non-working day, it moves to the following working day at 09:00 local time.

4.3 Suspension of API and dashboard access takes effect at 23:59 UTC on Day 15 if the balance remains unpaid. Suspension notices are sent no later than 48 hours before that time.

4.4 Accounts holding a prepaid credit balance are excluded from 4.1 to 4.3 until that balance is exhausted or 30 days have passed, whichever is sooner.

4.5 EXCEPTION. Where the outstanding amount is below £40.00 or the equivalent in the account currency, the account is not suspended under 4.3 and instead remains in Payment Recovery until the balance is cleared, provided that no more than two prior suspensions have been recorded against the account in the preceding 180 days.

4.6 Accounts on enterprise terms with a named account manager must not be suspended under this section without written approval from the Billing Lead. Approval requests are logged on form BA-F-17 and must state the reason, the outstanding amount, and the date of the last successful payment.

4.7 Customer contact during Payment Recovery is limited to one automated email per retry attempt, plus one manual call on Day 10 where a telephone number is held.

3. Priority classification

3.1 Incidents are assigned one of four priorities at logging, based on impact (number of users affected) and urgency (business function affected).

3.2 P1: whole site or more than 150 users unable to work, or any incident affecting payroll, dispatch or customer invoicing systems.

3.3 P2: more than 25 users affected, or a single critical application unavailable to a department.

3.4 P3: individual users or small groups affected, with a workaround available.

3.5 P4: cosmetic issues and general requests with no operational impact.

4. Response and resolution targets

4.1 Response targets are measured in elapsed clock hours from the time the incident is logged in the service desk tool (ref: SDT).

4.2 Resolution targets for P1 and P2 are measured in business days, excluding weekends and public holidays observed in England. For P3, resolution is measured in business days. For P4, resolution is measured in calendar days.

4.3 Targets are as follows:
  P1: response 30 minutes; resolution 1 business day.
  P2: response 2 hours; resolution 3 business days.
  P3: response 1 business day; resolution 5 business days.
  P4: response 3 business days; resolution 20 calendar days.

4.4 Target clock is paused while status is "Awaiting User" and resumes when the user replies or after 2 business days, whichever is sooner.

5. Exceptions

5.1 A P2 incident may be reclassified as P1 by the Duty Service Manager where a third-party supplier outage prevents a workaround, provided the reclassification is recorded in SDT before the response target expires.

5.2 Where an incident spans a public holiday, the holiday does not count against the target only if the incident was logged on or before the working day preceding that holiday.

5.3 Breaches caused by a delay in the Change Advisory Board approval process are excluded from SLA breach reporting, subject to written sign-off by the Head of IT Operations.

6. Breach reporting

6.1 All breaches are reviewed weekly by the Service Delivery Lead and summarised for the operations team lead, who determines whether a service credit or remedial action is required.

Document reference: PDS/POL/014
Version 3.2 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Review due 1 September 2028

1. Scope

1.1 This policy applies to applications for householder planning permission, listed building consent for minor works, and certificates of lawfulness submitted through the Council's online planning portal.

1.2 It sets out the minimum documents required before an application is registered and the timescales for the validation decision.

2. Validation Timescale

2.1 A validation decision shall be issued within five (5) working days of receipt of a complete application fee and submission.

2.2 For the purposes of this policy, "working day" means any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday, a bank holiday in England and Wales, or a day on which the Council offices are closed under clause 2.4.

2.3 Working days are counted from the day following receipt. Where the sixth day falls on a non-working day, the deadline moves to the next working day.

2.4 The Council offices are closed for the purposes of this clause on the days notified in the Council's annual calendar. Closure days notified after 1 July in any year shall not affect deadlines already running.

3. Required Documents

3.1 Every application shall include:
(a) a completed application form, reference HH/1 (rev. 4);
(b) location plan at a scale of 1:1250 or 1:2500, showing the site outlined in red;
(c) existing and proposed elevations at a scale of not less than 1:100;
(d) the fee calculated under the Town and Country Planning (Fees for Applications) Regulations.

3.2 Applications affecting a conservation area shall additionally include a Heritage Statement of no more than 1,500 words.

4. Incomplete Applications

4.1 Where an application lacks a document listed in clause 3.1, the validation officer shall write to the applicant within the period in clause 2.1 identifying each missing item.

4.2 The application shall not be registered until all items are received.

5. Exceptions

5.1 Clause 2.1 shall not apply where the application relates to a site subject to an open enforcement notice, in which case the validation officer shall refer the file to the Planning Enforcement Team within two (2) working days.

5.2 Clause 3.1(c) may be waived by the Head of Planning Services where the proposal is a rear extension not exceeding 3 metres in depth and the applicant supplies a written justification approved under this clause. Waivers shall be recorded on the file with the approving officer's initials and date.

6. Records

6.1 Validation decisions, waivers and referrals shall be logged in the Uniform case management system against the application reference.

4. Leak allowance: eligibility and calculation

4.1 A leak allowance may be considered where an underground supply leak is reported by the customer or identified by the Company, is on the customer's side of the boundary valve, and is repaired by the Company or its contractor.

4.2 Allowances are calculated on excess consumption above the property baseline. The baseline is the mean daily consumption over the 12 billing periods before the leak report. Where fewer than six periods are available, the regional average for the property band is used (Band C: 0.27 m³/day).

4.3 Excess volume is metered consumption from the leak report date to the repair date, less baseline for the same number of days, rounded down to the nearest whole cubic metre.

4.4 The allowance rate is £1.42 per m³ for excess volume up to 100 m³, and £0.85 per m³ thereafter. No allowance is payable where excess volume is below 5 m³.

4.5 Exception: where repair is delayed beyond 10 working days by a delay attributable to the Company, the period used under clause 4.3 is capped at 10 working days from the report date. Weekends and public holidays are not working days for this purpose. This exception applies only where the job sheet carries reason code CD or CA with a delay note.

4.6 Estimated reads are not used under clause 4.3 unless an actual customer read was confirmed within the 30 days before the leak report.

4.7 The assessor must record the calculation reference (format LA-YYYY-NNNN) against the account before any credit is applied.

Smart meter reads for 212 supply points in the Eastfield and Harrowmere postcode areas were not loaded into the billing platform on the scheduled run.
